walkthroughs.body_html:
Light refracts when it crosses into a new medium because it changes speed.

When light enters glass from air, it slows down. If it hits at an angle, the part that enters first slows first — and the whole ray bends.

Rule of thumb: going into an optically denser medium, light bends towards the normal. Coming out, it bends away.

The refractive index n tells you how much a material slows light. Air ≈ 1.0, water ≈ 1.33, glass ≈ 1.5, diamond ≈ 2.4.

Higher n means light travels more slowly inside that material and bends more sharply at the boundary.

That's why a diamond sparkles so much — it bends light strongly. 💎

A converging lens (fat in the middle) bends parallel rays to meet at a focal point. It's used in cameras, magnifying glasses and the human eye.

A diverging lens (thin in the middle) spreads parallel rays apart so they appear to come from a focal point behind the lens.

The distance from the lens to its focal point is the focal length, measured in metres.

mcqs.q: A ray of light passes from air into glass at an angle. Which way does it bend?
options: Away from the normal
Towards the normal
Along the surface
It doesn't bend
Thinner in the middle than at the edges
Fatter in the middle than at the edges
Flat on both sides
A perfect sphere

mcqs.q: Why does light bend when it enters a denser medium like glass?
options: Because the medium is denser, it physically blocks part of the light and forces it to turn.
Because it slows down — the change in speed at the boundary causes the wavefront to bend (towards the normal).
Because gravity in the glass pulls the light down.
It reflects them back the way they came.

mcqs.q: How do you see a non-luminous object like a book?
options: Your eyes send out beams of vision that hit the book and let you see it.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
Light from a source reflects off the book and enters your eyes.
It reflects them back the way they came.

mcqs.q: What does a concave lens do to parallel rays of light?
options: It converges them to a focal point in front of the lens.
It diverges them — they spread out as if from a virtual focal point behind the lens.
It reflects them back the way they came.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
